records.title: Dispatch Loom
records.subtitle: Dispatch reconciliation tool
records.summary: Personally designed and built a tool for dispatch reconciliation, using a Python parser and SQL checks. Gathered requirements from warehouse supervisors and explained validation failures. Operators compared an overnight spreadsheet with a daily export; the tool kept empty rows visible and warned when the source file arrived late. The supervisor made final dispatch decisions. The reconciliation-time improvement was a team result, not solely attributable to Ada.

records.title: Reconciliation time reduction
records.subtitle: Harbor Tools
records.summary: Team result: Dispatch Loom reduced reconciliation time from 5 hours to 2 hours per week over six weekly runs. Ada's contribution was the parser and checks; coworkers also changed their checking habits. Delivery speed was not measured, and the earlier 50% time-saved figure was incorrect.

decisions.reason: The name, profile description, and stated denials are supported by the transcript.
The role, employer, dates, personal project work, and training are supported. The time improvement is correctly described as a team result.

The source says operators preferred a visible warning when the source file arrived late; it does not establish that the tool itself warned them. The project summary asserts that behavior as completed functionality.
The training count, two workshops, handbook, and unknown exact workshop dates are supported; the Dispatch Loom context connects the achievement to Harbor Tools.

The 5-to-2-hours-per-week reduction over six weekly runs, team attribution, Ada’s stated contribution, coworker behavior changes, and corrections about the 50% figure and delivery speed are supported.
The source supports Ada’s use of Python to build the parser, and explicitly places Python in the Data tools skill category.
The source supports Ada’s use of SQL to write checks and explicitly places SQL in the Data tools skill category.
The source says Ada used PostgreSQL for the production database and includes PostgreSQL in the Data tools category.
The source says Ada used Git for version control and includes Git in the Collaboration category.
Personal coworker training is supported, and coworker training is explicitly included in the Collaboration skill category.
The degree, field, institution, and dates match the source.
The certificate and date are supported; the source identifies it as fictional course completion rather than a professional license.
